text:
alex_support: Hi @maria_billing — customer (AcmeAnalytics) opened a ticket: their Dedicated pool 'redwood-prod-us-west-2' shows ~1,200 reserved GPU hours consumed over the last 24h while API token burn is ~12k tokens. They say there were no large batch jobs. Can you triage?

maria_billing: Thanks, Alex. Can you share the pool id and any request ids? Also need the invoice line and sample hourly meter rows if available.

alex_support: Pool id: pool-rw-usw2-7b4. Ticket ID: #C-90512. Quick snippet from the hourly meter we pulled:
```
2026-03-16T00:00Z pool=pool-rw-usw2-7b4 reserved_gpu_hours=50 token_burn=450
2026-03-16T01:00Z pool=pool-rw-usw2-7b4 reserved_gpu_hours=48 token_burn=300
2026-03-16T02:00Z pool=pool-rw-usw2-7b4 reserved_gpu_hours=52 token_burn=200
```
Customer says no long-lived warmup or maintenance windows.

ken_sre: Tagging in. First suspicion: warmup instances or pre-provisioned burst nodes being double-counted in reserved_hours metric. Can we check instance lifecycle events against metering? @deploy-bot do we have deploy/warmup events for that pool?

deploy-bot: deploy events for pool-rw-usw2-7b4 between 2026-03-15T22:00Z and 2026-03-16T04:00Z:
- warmup: instance-443 start 2026-03-15T22:10Z
- warmup: instance-444 start 2026-03-16T00:05Z
- preemptible-scan: instance-450 probe 2026-03-16T01:50Z

maria_billing: Hmm, warmup looks minimal. Another angle: Are burst (overcommit) hours being attributed to reserved pool even when billed as burst? If fallback routing sent traffic to another capacity tier that still billed against the reserved commit, that could inflate reserved_hours.

sarah_customer: From our side we only had a handful of test calls and one scheduled batch at 00:30 for ~2 minutes. We didn't run anything heavy. Our dashboard shows very low model call counts.

ken_sre: Could be a metering aggregation bug where per-instance partial-hours are rounded up and then summed instead of being prorated across the pool. Example: two instances running 15m each -> counts as 2 * 1h instead of 0.5h total. I'll pull the raw instance lifecycle and rounding code.

maria_billing: Can you also check invoice line mapping? The invoice shows 1,184 reserved hours on 2026-03-16 for that account. Dashboard reserve-meter shows 1,190. The difference is small but both are orders of magnitude above token burn.

ken_sre: Repro steps I'm running: 1) fetch instance_lifecycle for pool-rw-usw2-7b4 2) compute per-instance hours with current rounding logic 3) cross-check with billing-aggregator output and token-meter. If we see rounding as culprit, we'll need a hotfix and corrective billing adjustment.

alex_support: Customer wants an ETA and whether SLA credits will apply. They asked to pause auto-scaling until we confirm.

maria_billing: If it's a metering bug we will apply pro-rated SLA credits and open a billing dispute for the 2026-03-16 line day. I'll prepare the provisional credit template.

ken_sre: Quick findings: initial check shows ~14 instances with very short lifetimes (2–10 minutes) during that window. Current aggregator does ceil(instance_uptime_hours) per instance before summing. That matches the symptom. Patch idea: change to sum fractional hours then ceil at pool level.

maria_billing: Good catch. What's the rollout risk? Any DB migration?

ken_sre: Low risk code change in billing-aggregator service. Need a small migration to re-run the daily aggregation for affected pools for last 7 days. No schema changes. I'll open PR and request an emergency deploy.

alex_support: I'll tell the customer we're triaging, pausing autoscale on their pool per their request, and will follow up with provisional credit if the fix confirms overcount.

sarah_customer: Thanks — please keep us updated. We rely on predictable reserved hours for budgeting.

maria_billing: Next steps: ken opens PR and links runbook; I prepare the provisional credit (estimate: refund of ~1,050 reserved hours * unit_rate until final reconciliation). We'll hold final invoice adjustments until aggregation re-run completes. Escalating to billing lead for sign-off.

ken_sre: PR #2749 opened: change aggregator to pool-level rounding + replay job. Triggering replay for pool-rw-usw2-7b4 for 2026-03-10..2026-03-16. I'll post results in this thread when done.

maria_billing: Thanks — ping @billing-lead and @legal for any contract concerns.

alex_support: Noted. Marking this high priority.

deploy-bot: replay job started (job-8891). ETA 35m.

ken_sre: Replay finished. Aggregator delta: reserved_hours before=1,192 after=138. Billing delta ~ -1,054 hours. Will prepare final adjustment and sync with maria for crediting.

maria_billing: Confirmed. Preparing provisional credit now and emailing customer. Will update ticket #C-90512 with credit details and next invoice impact. Closing loop when legal signs off. :white_check_mark:

sarah_customer: Appreciate the quick work.

alex_support: Closing internal thread; will reopen if anything else pops up.
